citation.biblCit: Laupichler, M. C., Aster, A., Haverkamp, N., & Raupach, T. (2023). Development of the "Scale for the assessment of non-experts' AI literacy" – An exploratory factor analysis. Computers in Human Behavior Reports, 12, 100338. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbr.2023.100338

stdyInfo.abstract: Self-assessment scale of AI literacy for non-experts, i.e. people without formal AI or computer science training. 31 "I can …" statements, rated on a six-point agreement scale (the scale of the latest source, S1 of Laupichler et al. 2023; the original paper used seven points), cover three factors: Technical Understanding, Critical Appraisal and Practical Application. The items come from a Delphi study and were reduced from 39 by exploratory factor analysis with an online sample; the German version is the authors' systematic translation (Laupichler, Aster, Perschewski & Schleiss 2023).
